question: How can one machine be the hottest and coldest place in the universe?
answer: At 150 million degrees, no material can hold the plasma, so magnets hold it floating inside the hollow ring. Those superconducting magnets keep their magnetic properties only when chilled to −269 °C. So in ITER, the hottest thing is held in place by the coldest thing.
